subject.title: fix(desktop): notifications use native macOS and Windows services

question: Should OpenClaw temporarily ship the fork-pinned notification backend together with the Rust 1.90 and macOS 13 floors, or wait for the upstream dependency path?
rationale: The patch combines the desired user-visible fix with a temporary build-time dependency trust choice and compatibility-floor changes that cannot be accepted from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Audit and accept temporarily
options.body: Audit the exact fork delta, document its removal condition, confirm the compatibility floors, obtain live platform proof, and then merge.

options.title: Wait for upstream
options.body: Pause until the upstream linking fix lands, then pin an upstream revision or release and avoid carrying a personal fork.

options.title: Retain the generic backend
options.body: Keep the existing backend until a native implementation can meet dependency, compatibility, and live-proof requirements without the temporary fork.

recommendation.title: Audit and accept temporarily
recommendation.body: Audit the exact fork delta, document its removal condition, confirm the compatibility floors, obtain live platform proof, and then merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the proposed desktop direction and is the strongest available candidate to decide the temporary dependency and supported-platform tradeoff.
